simple.meaning: פָּתִיל (pâthîyl) is a Hebrew object word meaning “twine.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 38:18. The surrounding context includes family, Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּתִיל (H6616) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: פָּתִיל (pâthîyl) / H6616 is traced through Genesis 38:18, Genesis 38:25, Exodus 28:28, Exodus 28:37 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He said, “What pledge will I give you?”

timeline.evidenceText: He said, “What pledge will I give you?”
When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “I am with child by the man who owns these.” She also said, “Please discern whose these are—the signet, and the cords, and the staff.”

They shall bind the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate may not swing out from the ephod.
You shall put it on a lace of blue, and it shall be on the sash. It shall be on the front of the sash.
They beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into wires, to work it in with the blue, the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen, the work of the skillful workman.

They bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not come loose from the ephod, as Yahweh commanded Moses.
They tied to it a lace of blue, to fasten it on the turban above, as Yahweh commanded Moses.
“Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them that they should make themselves fringes
Every open vessel, which has no covering bound on it, is unclean.

Now she had an ambush waiting in the inner room. She said to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He broke the cords as a flax thread is broken when it touches the fire. So his strength was not known.
He brought me there; and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate.

definitions.usage: bound, bracelet, lace, line, ribband, thread, wire.
definitions.full: H6616. pathil מָּתִיל noun masculine Judg 16:9 cord, thread ( twisted ); — absolute ׳פ Num 19:15 ; construct מְּתִיל Judg 16:9 +; suffix מְּתִילֶ֑ךָ Gen 38:18 ; plural מְּתִילִים 38:25 , מְּתִילִם Exod 39:3 ; — cord (from which seal was hung) Gen 38:18 , 25 (J), נְעֹרֶת ׳פ Judg 16:9 (simile), ׳פ מִּשְׁתִּים Ezek 40:3 (as measuring line); ׳פ תְּכֵלֶת , for fastening, Exod 28:28 , 37 ; 39:21 , 31 ; Num 15:38 , compare מָּתִיל alone 19:15 (perhaps gloss, see Di); threads (of gold) in ephod Exod 39:3 (all P).
